episodes.170080: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the afternoon and evening of the 21st. The thunderstorms were high-based, and had a deep layer of dry air between the cloud bases and the ground, which resulted in an enhancement of the downdraft momentum due to evaporative cooling into the dry air. A similar environment was in place on the 22nd, with strong to severe thunderstorms once again developing in the afternoon and evening. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170670: Evening sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.170687: Summertime Seabreeze convection resulted in a funnel cloud and a report of severe winds.
episodes.170739: Southeast New Mexico was on the eastern periphery of an upper ridge. Upper level disturbances were moving along the eastern edge of the ridge. There was increased mid-level moisture and lift and elevated instability across the area. Low-level moisture was also present along with lingering outflow boundaries from previous thunderstorms. These conditions resulted in a thunderstorm that produced hail in Eddy County.
episodes.170793: Scattered thunderstorms develop across the northern mountains during the early afternoon of July 22m 2022 in response to a decaying Mesoscale Convective Vortex (MCV) crossing the area. One of these storms produced marginally severe hail in Lycoming County.
episodes.171056: A slow moving cold front was the main culprit behind showers and storms that prevailed across West Virginia between July 21st and 23rd. Strong to severe storms thrived during the afternoon hours, and often caused blown down trees and power lines from damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171098: A severe storm damaged trees in Dodge County.
episodes.171125: Several clusters of storms developed across central Mississippi on the evening of July 21st. These storms evolved into two loosely organized line segments that produced wind damage across the area. Numerous trees were blown down along with several power lines.
episodes.171127: Slow moving thunderstorms on the afternoon of July 22nd resulted in flash flooding in Covington County near Collins.
episodes.171185: A series of cold fronts and disturbances passed through southeast Ohio from July 20th to 23rd, with daily afternoon showers and thunderstorms ensuing. Storms that occurred from the 20th to 22nd resulted in some minor tree damage, but the more substantial activity arrived on the 23rd, when trees and power lines were knocked down.
episodes.171324: A warm front crossed the region during the morning of the 21st. A cold front and strong upper level disturbance then crossed the region during the afternoon and evening. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and persisted into the evening. Isolated severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.171333: Strong thunderstorms produced isolated wind damage and some flash flooding.
episodes.171343: A pair of isolated severe wind gusts, likely associated with heat burst activity, were recorded in southern Dawson County on this Thursday evening. A subtle upper level shortwave disturbance embedded in northwesterly flow moved out of Wyoming and into western Nebraska during the daytime hours. At the surface, a trough axis was draped from central North Dakota southward through the Nebraska panhandle. This surface boundary served as a focus for mid-late afternoon thunderstorm development over western Nebraska, which trekked southeast with time, following an axis of increased instability. The complex of storms pushed southeast out of the Sandhills and into South Central Nebraska during the evening hours, with activity primarily affecting northern and western portions of the local coverage area between 8:30 PM and midnight CDT. ||By the time this activity moved into the area, diminishing MUCAPE values were around 1500-2000 J/kg with deeper layer shear around 30-35 knots. Though large hail was a possibility, the main severe weather threat was damaging wind gusts, with the 00Z July 22 sounding from North Platte showing a deep, well-mixed layer just off the surface. The strongest portion of this line of storms tracked into Dawson County between 8:30-9:30 PM CDT, but sub-severe gusts generally peaked only between 45-55 MPH, though one gust of 57 MPH was recorded near Cozad. As this activity continued southeastward during the late evening hours, it showed an overall weakening trend. But then, between 10:55-11:20 PM CDT, measured gusts exceeding 60 MPH were recorded on the backside of this decaying convection...including 64 MPH near Johnson Lake and 62 MPH at the Lexington Airport AWOS. Downdraft CAPE values in the area through the evening hours were between 1000-1500 J/kg. The time of day and environment were favorable for heat bursts. In this area of decaying convection between 10-11:30 PM CDT, the Lexington AWOS reflected a temperature rise from 71 to 83 F, and a drop in dewpoint from 67 to 54 F, corresponding to the development of the severe southerly winds.
episodes.171428: A weak disturbance moved through Northeastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon. The environment was unstable enough to support some severe thunderstorms that produced damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.171429: A weak disturbance moved through Central New York during the afternoon. The environment was unstable enough to support some severe thunderstorms that produced damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.171490: A thunderstorm became severe as it tracked across eastern Bennett County. The storm produced large hail northeast of Vetal.
episodes.171722: A line of severe thunderstorms moved through portions of southwest and central Nebraska during the evening of July 21, resulting in 60 mph winds and large hail.
episodes.171842: A few strong to isolated severe storms impacted NE FL as both sea breeze fronts converged near the US 301 corridor late in the afternoon and early evening over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.171905: A meso-scale convective system developed out of afternoon thunderstorms initiated along a frontal boundary in northern Alabama and Georgia on the 21st. That MCS raced south across southern Alabama and Mississippi during the overnight hours, moving across the local area on the morning of the 22nd. It produced severe winds across marine areas.
episodes.171906: A meso-scale convective system (MCS) developed out of afternoon thunderstorms initiated along a frontal boundary in northern Alabama and Georgia on the 21st. That MCS raced south across southern Alabama and Mississippi during the overnight hours, moving across the local area on the morning of the 22nd. There was also flash flooding in the Baton Rouge Metro due to the portion of the squall line associated with the MCS slowing down as it moved through there. In addition, a home and junior high gym caught fire after lightning strikes. No injuries reported with those fires.
episodes.172046: During the afternoon to early evening hours, a disturbance moved over the High Plains creating isolated to scattered thunderstorms that produced multiple tornadoes, up to ping pong ball sized hail, and damaging winds with gusts up to 90 mph.  The wind damage occurred in Decatur, Sheridan and Graham counties, with damage to an airport hanger in the city of Hoxie, damage to an outbuilding and utility trailer, and numerous large tree limbs downed. The largest hail was reported in southern Logan County while the strongest winds were reported in Hoxie with the damage to the airplane hanger.
episodes.172048: Isolated severe storms resulted in several reports of damaging wind gusts which resulted in several downed trees and tree limbs and power outages.
episodes.172096: A cluster of thunderstorms developed over the Nebraska Panhandle and Northeast Colorado during the afternoon hours. These storms moved east-southeast into extreme Southwest Nebraska producing thunderstorm wind gusts up to 62 mph in Dundy, Hitchcock, and Red Willow counties.
episodes.172097: During the evening hours, an isolated thunderstorm developed over Northeast Colorado moving southeast across Yuma County. The storm reached it's peak strength in the southeast corner of the county near the town of Idalia, Colorado where it produced nickel sized hail.
episodes.172209: An upper level short wave trough moving through the region resulted in severe thunderstorms developing over south central North Dakota. Initially, a severe thunderstorm quickly developed and moved through the Bismarck and Lincoln areas of Burleigh County, with a second storm developing right behind the first one following a similar track. There was a report of tennis ball size hail in the north side of Bismarck, with most locations seeing quarter to golf ball size hail. The area around the Bismarck Airport received no hail. Where hail fell there was widespread roof and vehicle damage. Additional severe storms developed to the south and east, resulting in many reports of crop damage. Although hail was the main threat with these storms, one storm produced reported 65 mph wind gusts near Zeeland in McIntosh County.
episodes.172236: A MCS over Tennessee during the morning hours of July 21 pushed an outflow boundary into north Alabama in the afternoon. The air mass was very unstable south of the outflow boundary with surface based CAPE 3500-4500 J/kg and DCAPE 1300-1500 J/kg.  The storms that initiated in the afternoon organized into QLCS that produced widespread damaging winds, large hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.172419: Thunderstorms developed along the Mogollon Rim over to the White Mountains during the afternoon of the 21st. High pressure centered over the northern portion of the state promoted weak east/northeast steering flow, which helped thunderstorms to propagate toward the west/southwest. Sufficient moisture (PWATs around 1.3-1.4) and high instability (CAPE around 1,000-1,500 J/kg) provided a favorable environment for strong to severe thunderstorms capable of producing locally heavy rainfall across southern Gila County. By early evening, strong to severe thunderstorms pushed into the Globe area producing damaging winds, hail, and flash flooding in the area. No injuries were reported.
episodes.172440: A waterspout moved onshore from Sabine Lake into Motiva. The slow moving landspout moved through the refinery without causing damage.
episodes.172441: A waterspout developed over Sabine Lake and moved across Pleasure Island into Motiva.
episodes.172529: An area of low pressure brought severe thunderstorms to north-central and northeastern South Dakota during the late evening hours. The storms produced mainly quarter size hail, with one report of golf ball size hail 4 miles north of Eureka.
episodes.172629: Microbursts and associated outflows yielded strong wind gusts from portions of Utah's West Desert region into portions of the Wasatch Front.
episodes.172683: Scattered thunderstorms moved southwest across Cochise County during the afternoon and evening where they produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.172684: Scattered thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. One storm produced large hail in Patagonia.
episodes.172697: Scattered thunderstorms developed with a strengthening low-level jet during the overnight hours.  With MUCAPE of around 1000 J/kg and 30 knots of effective shear, isolated storms produced up to quarter size hail.
episodes.172698: Scattered thunderstorms developed with a strengthening low-level jet during the overnight hours. With MUCAPE of around 1000 J/kg and 30 knots of effective shear, isolated storms produced up to quarter size hail and damaging wind.
episodes.172717: Isolated severe thunderstorms over southeast Lake Michigan arrived onshore and produced periodic wind damage and hail.
episodes.172718: Isolated severe thunderstorms over southeast Lake Michigan arrived onshore and produced periodic wind damage and hail.
episodes.172772: An upper high was located over New Mexico with some deep low and mid level moisture trapped under it over the Sacramento Mountains.  Training thunderstorms over the eastern slopes of the Sacramento Mountains brought up to 4 inches of rain to the area.
episodes.172846: A severe thunderstorm formed in Barnes county during the evening hours, then moved east into Cass County. This storm primarily produced large hail.
